newsitem.title: CHINA: China says troops ready for Hong Kong duties.
newsitem.headline: China says troops ready for Hong Kong duties.

text.p: Soldiers from China's People's Liberation Army are fully ready to begin their duties as the new Hong Kong garrison after the British colony returns to Chinese rule in July, the official China Daily said on Saturday.

Soldiers training across the Hong Kong border in China's southern city of Shenzhen had vowed not to indulge in business activities after deployment in the territory and were determined to win the loyalty of its people, the newspaper said.
"After July 1, the garrison troops will make Hong Kong their hometown and the local people their family members," it said.
"We deeply understand our lofty mission and enormous responsibility," said Major-General Liu Zhenwu, commander of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Garrison.

The arrival of Chinese soldiers in Hong Kong has been viewed with concern by some of the free-wheeling territory's residents, particularily since the crushing of pro-democracy demonstrations in Beijing in 1989 by Liberation Army troops.

The new garrison was determined to respect the Hong Kong government after the handover of power at midnight on June 30, China Daily quoted officers as saying, adding that the soldiers would be barred from entry to Hong Kong's business world.
"We promise to shut the door on any commercial activities after we go to Hong Kong," said garrison political commissar Major-General Xiong Ziren as saying.
